chunks: He said: My father narrated to us from Sa'd b. 'Abdullah from Muhammad b. 'Isa b. 'Ubayd al-Yaqtini from al-Hasan b. Muhammad b. Bashar,

he said: An 'ammi shaykh from Qati'at al-Rabi' narrated to me — one whose word was accepted — he said: He said to me: I have indeed seen some of those who acknowledge the virtue of a man from the People of this House, and I have never seen anyone like him in his asceticism and virtue. He said: I said: Who? And how did you see him?

He said: Al-Sindi b. Shahik gathered us — eighty men of renown attributed to goodness — in the days [of al-Sindi], and brought us in to Musa b. Ja'far (upon them both be peace). Al-Sindi said to us: O you people! Look at this man — has anything happened to him? For the people allege that he has been treated wrongly, and they make much ado about that. This is his residence and his furnishings — spacious for him and not restricted. The Commander of the Faithful has not intended any harm for him. He is only waiting for him to come so the Commander of the Faithful may converse with him. Here he is, healthy, with ample provision in all his affairs — so ask him. He said: And we had no concern except to look at the man and at his virtue and his character.

Then he said: As for what he mentioned regarding the spaciousness and the like, it is as he mentioned. Except that I inform you, O people, that I was fed poison in nine dates, and that I will turn green tomorrow, and the day after tomorrow I will die. He said: So I looked at al-Sindi b. Shahik, and he was shuddering and shaking like a palm leaf.
Al-Hasan said: This shaykh was from the best of the Sunnis — a truthful shaykh, whose word was accepted, and who was very much trusted by the people.

key_terms.أمير المؤمنين: Commander of the Faithful — title used here for Abbasid Caliph Harun al-Rashid
key_terms.أهل البيت: People of the House — the family of Prophet Muhammad (s)
key_terms.السندي بن شاهك: al-Sindi b. Shahik — Abbasid prison warden who held Imam Musa al-Kadhim in captivity
key_terms.العامة: The general populace — commonly refers to the Sunni community

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Musa al-Kadhim announce his poisoning before his martyrdom in the prison of al-Sindi b. Shahik?
ai.summary: This hadith preserves a Sunni eyewitness account of Imam Musa al-Kadhim's (as) final days in the prison of al-Sindi b. Shahik during the reign of Harun al-Rashid. Al-Sindi gathered eighty notable men to demonstrate that the Imam was being treated well, hoping to counter public accusations of mistreatment. However, the Imam himself calmly announced that he had been poisoned through nine dates, would turn green the next day, and would die the day after. The narrator observed al-Sindi visibly shaking upon hearing this pronouncement. The account is significant because it comes from a trusted Sunni narrator, lending cross-sectarian credibility to the historical record of the Imam's martyrdom. Al-Hasan b. Muhammad b. Bashar vouches for the narrator's reliability, noting he was among the most trustworthy of the Sunni community.

en.bilal-muhammad: He said: My father narrated to me from Sa`d b. `Abdullah from Muhammad b. `Isa b. `Ubayd al-Yaqtini from al-Hasan b. Muhammad b. Bashar.

He said: An `ammi shaykh from Qati`atul Rabi`, whose words were accepted, narrated to me that he had seen people declare the virtue of a man from the People of this House. [He said:] I have never seen anyone as ascetic and as virtuous as him. He said: I said: Who? How did you see him?

He said: One day, eighty of us – men of renown and goodness – gathered to al-Sindi b. Shahik, and we visited Musa b. Ja`far (as). So, a-Sindi said to us: O you! Look to this man – has anything happened to him? For surely, the people allege that he has been treated wrongly, and they make much ado about that. This is his house and his furnishings; it is expansive for him and not narrow. The commander of the faithful does not want any harm to come to him. Surely, he is only waiting for him to come and for the commander of the faithful to converse with him. Here he is, he is healthy, and all his affairs are widely available to him. He said: We had no concerns, so we only looked to the man and to his virtue and his character.

Then, he said: As for what he mentioned regarding the wideness [of available things] and its like, then it is as he has mentioned. Except, I will inform you, O people, that I was fed poison in nine dates, and that I will turn green tomorrow, and that after tomorrow I will die. He said: So, I looked to al-Sindi b. Shahik, and he was shuddering and shaking like a ringworm.
Al-Hasan said: This shaykh was from the best of the `amma. He was trustworthy, and his words were accepted. He was trusted very much by the people.
